witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 61.10
div.ab: Si quis dapifer uel prepositus uel minister placitum domini sui contramandet, ita sit, quicquid dominus eius dicat, si redierit et placitum aduersarii sui fractum esse uelit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 581 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: gescheitert durch Nichterscheinen des Gegners, der aber durch den Verwalter abbestellt gewesen
failed through the non-appearance of the opponent, who had, however, been called off by the steward
Vgl. Gl Truchsess 4a; Adelsbeamte 11—se{46}—61, 11 quorum bis eius am Rande Rs
Cf. Gl Truchsess 4a; Adelsbeamte 11—se{46}—61, 11 quorum to eius in the margin Rs

div.ab: If any steward or reeve or servant countermands his lord's plea, let it be so, whatever his lord says, if he returns and wishes his adversary's plea to be broken.
